images.caption: PSII oxidises water and reduces plastoquinone; its H⁺ collect in the lumen and leave through ATP synthase
images.credit: Shevela, Kern, Govindjee & Messinger 2023, Photosynth Res 156:279, Fig. 1 (CC BY 4.0)
images.note: The whole chunk in one figure: both PSII equations, lumen H⁺, and the link to ATP synthase.

images.caption: Plant PSII in the thylakoid: Mn₄CaO₅ → YZ → P680 → Pheo → QA → QB → PQH₂
images.credit: Shevela, Kern, Govindjee & Messinger 2023, Photosynth Res 156:279, Fig. 3a (CC BY 4.0); deck file photos/7-membrane.png

images.caption: C. B. van Niel, 1964. From sulfur bacteria (H₂S → S) he inferred that plant O₂ comes from water
images.credit: Marion S. Trikosko, 13 Jan 1964 (detail), Library of Congress, U.S. News & World Report collection; public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
images.note: His comparison CO₂ + 2 H₂A → (CH₂O) + H₂O + 2 A dates from 1931; the photo is from his National Medal of Science.

images.caption: Sam Ruben (left) and Martin Kamen: with ¹⁸O-water they showed in 1941 that photosynthetic O₂ comes from water
images.credit: Ruben: Seaborg Archive, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, via UC Berkeley College of Chemistry (credit for teaching); Kamen: Donald Cooksey, 1938 (detail), public domain, Wikimedia Commons
images.note: Paper: Ruben, Randall, Kamen & Hyde 1941, J Am Chem Soc 63:877. Kamen photo: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Martin-kamen_by_donald-cooksey-in-front-of-60-inch-9bac2f.jpg

images.caption: Deisenhofer, Huber and Michel: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1988 for the first reaction-centre structure
images.credit: Photos from the Nobel Foundation archive, nobelprize.org (© Nobel Prize Outreach); left to right Deisenhofer, Huber, Michel
images.note: Structure paper: Deisenhofer, Epp, Miki, Huber & Michel 1985, Nature 318:618 (purple bacterium Rhodopseudomonas viridis).

images.caption: The purple-bacterial reaction centre in its membrane (red lines): chlorophylls green, quinones orange, cytochrome haems pink
images.credit: David S. Goodsell, RCSB PDB Molecule of the Month, Oct 2001, doi:10.2210/rcsb_pdb/mom_2001_10 (CC BY 4.0); PDB 1PRC; right half of the illustration
images.note: The structure that won the 1988 prize; the same RC design returns in PSII.

images.caption: PSII dimer at 1.9 Å, side view; orange balls are bound water molecules
images.credit: Umena, Kawakami, Shen & Kamiya 2011, Nature 473:55, Fig. 1a (PDB 3ARC, replaced in 2014 by 3WU2)

images.caption: PSII reaction-centre cofactors of both monomers; Mn cluster at the top (lumen), quinones at the bottom (stroma)
images.credit: David S. Goodsell, RCSB PDB Molecule of the Month, Nov 2004, doi:10.2210/rcsb_pdb/mom_2004_11 (CC BY 4.0); PDB 1S5L (Ferreira et al. 2004, Science 303:1831)
images.note: Stand-in for Ferreira 2004, whose own figures are blocked; small (752 px).

images.caption: Electron path inside the PSII structure, from water at Mn₄CaO₅ via P680 and pheophytin to QB and PQH₂
images.credit: Shevela, Kern, Govindjee & Messinger 2023, Photosynth Res 156:279, Fig. 5b (CC BY 4.0)
images.note: Distances in Å; the inset zooms into the Mn₄CaO₅ site.

images.caption: Primary charge separation: excited P680 hands an electron to pheophytin, leaving P680⁺
images.credit: Shevela, Kern, Govindjee & Messinger 2023, Photosynth Res 156:279, Fig. 6a (CC BY 4.0); deck file photos/7-shevela-a.png

images.caption: Cofactor chain on a redox-potential axis with step times: ~3 ps to Pheo, ~250 ps to QA
images.credit: Shevela, Kern, Govindjee & Messinger 2023, Photosynth Res 156:279, Fig. 6b (CC BY 4.0)
images.note: The energy-and-time diagram the brief asked for: from water at the bottom to PQH₂ (1–20 ms).

images.caption: QB collects two electrons and two stromal H⁺, then leaves as PQH₂; inner circle: Kok cycle
images.credit: Shevela, Kern, Govindjee & Messinger 2023, Photosynth Res 156:279, Fig. 7 (CC BY 4.0)
images.note: The board's only Kok-cycle image; right column shows the QA–Fe–QB structures.

images.caption: Plastoquinone → plastoquinol chemistry; PSII side view; QA, QB sites and the channels to the PQ pool
images.credit: Van Eerden, Melo, Frederix, Periole & Marrink 2017, Nat Commun 8:15214, Fig. 1 (CC BY 4.0)

images.caption: The Mn₄CaO₅ cluster: four Mn, one Ca, five oxo bridges, four bound waters (bond lengths in Å)
images.credit: Umena, Kawakami, Shen & Kamiya 2011, Nature 473:55, Fig. 2b; deck file photos/7-cluster.png

images.caption: At the cluster: O₂ leaves, a new water enters, and a proton exits through a channel towards the lumen
images.credit: Bhowmick et al. 2023, Nature 617:629, Fig. 5 step iv (CC BY 4.0); deck file photos/7-channels.png
images.note: Proton (cyan), water (red dashed) and O₂ (red solid) paths from X-ray laser snapshots.
